element.description: One thing on a slide. Give 'type' plus the fields for that type; everything visual (fonts, colours, motion) is decided by the app.

id.description: Unique on the slide; cues and focus use it (e.g. 'knee'). Letters, digits, '_' and '-'. Generated if omitted.

area.description: Which region: 'left'/'right' in split, 'main'/'side' in wide. Optional; order decides otherwise.

rect.description: free layout only: [x, y, w, h] as fractions of the slide.

caption.description: A short line under the element.

hidden.description: Start invisible; reveal with a [[show id]] cue in the narration.

text.description: title: the title. markdown: CommonMark with tables, code and $inline$ / $$display$$ TeX.

subtitle.description: title: a line under the title.

kicker.description: title: a small line above it ('Lesson 1').

src.description: image: a local file path or an http(s) URL (downloaded and kept with the deck).

fit.description: image: contain (default) shows all of it.

callouts.description: image: labels with leader lines, laid out in gutters beside the image like an anatomy atlas. Measure positions with inspect_image first.

at.description: [x, y] point the leader touches, as fractions of the image (0,0 top-left).

box.description: [x, y, w, h] area to outline instead of a point, as fractions of the image.

detail.description: A sentence shown on hover and when focused.

mermaid.description: diagram: Mermaid source (flowchart, sequence, state, class, er, mindmap, block-beta, timeline…). Node ids become focus targets: [[focus flowId.nodeId]].

steps.description: diagram: node ids in the order the narration walks them; lets the user step with the arrow keys.

tex.description: math: TeX source without $ delimiters, e.g. \frac{a}{b}. Use aligned for several lines.

kind.description: chart: the kind, with data, x and y.

x.description: chart: field for categories / x axis.

y.description: chart: field for values / y axis.

series.description: chart: optional field that splits rows into coloured series.

vegaLite.description: chart: a complete Vega-Lite spec instead of kind/data/x/y, for anything else. Omit width, height and config.

rows.description: table: rows of cells (strings, numbers, booleans, null).

key.description: table: column whose values name rows for focus; default the first.

folder.description: gallery: show the images in this folder (their EXIF is shown on hover).

arrange.description: gallery: scatter (an organic pile, default), grid, or timeline by date taken.

places.description: map: the places to mark, in the order the narration visits them. Each is a focus target: [[focus journey.cairo]] flies the map there as the voice says the word.

id.description: Focus it with [[focus mapId.placeId]]; made from the label when omitted.

label.description: The name on the map; a few words.

at.description: [latitude, longitude] in degrees: [51.5074, -0.1278] is London. Latitude first.

detail.description: A sentence shown when the place is focused.

zoom.description: How close in to go for this place: 4 a country, 10 a city, 15 a street.

center.description: map: [latitude, longitude] of the middle; omit to frame the places.

zoom.description: map: 0 the world, 4 a country, 10 a city, 15 a street, 19 a doorway. Omit to fit the places.

route.description: map: draw a line from each place to the next, and number them: a journey, a route, a campaign.

answer.description: quiz: zero-based indexes of the correct options; omit for a poll.

slide.description: A slide: elements arranged by a layout, plus narration that is spoken and subtitled.

id.description: Stable id; putting a slide with an existing id replaces it. Generated from the title if omitted.

title.description: Heading shown at the top of the slide.

layout.description: Omit to have it chosen: one element fills the slide; a picture with text becomes wide (picture large); more become a grid.

narration.description: What is said over the slide, 2-5 sentences. Inline cues fire as the voice reaches them: [[focus el]] or [[focus el.part]] (shorthand [[el.part]]), [[zoom el x y w h]], [[show el]], [[hide el]], [[clear]].

advance.description: Move on by itself when the narration ends, or wait for the user. Default is the user's setting.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: What the user is looking at and what is in the deck: slides with their ids and titles, which of them have already been played, the current slide, what is focused on it, playback, voice budget, and whether the user has caught up with the newest slide.

tools.name: list_decks
tools.description: Saved presentations, newest first, with what each is about. Every one is a session you can reopen: describe_deck looks inside one, open_deck puts it back on the stage.

tools.name: new_deck
tools.description: Start a new, empty deck and show it. Do this first when the user asks about a new topic.

tools.name: open_deck
tools.description: Open a saved deck by id (from list_decks).

tools.name: put_slide
tools.description: Add a slide, or replace the slide with the same id. Returns once the slide has rendered, with any problems (a Mermaid syntax error, an image that failed to load, a cue at a missing part) and the parts you can focus. Build the first slide quickly and keep adding: the user watches earlier slides while you work.

after.description: Insert after this slide id, or "start". Omit to append (or, when replacing, to keep its place).

tools.name: update_slide
tools.description: Change part of a slide in place, for building it up live: set or replace elements by id, remove elements, or change title, layout, narration or advance. Changes animate in.

elements.description: Elements to add, or to replace when the id already exists.

tools.name: remove_slide
tools.description: Delete a slide.

tools.name: move_slide
tools.description: Move a slide to follow another, or to the start.

tools.name: go_to
tools.description: Show a slide now. Use sparingly: the user navigates too, and yanking them away mid-sentence is rude. Good for the first slide, or when they ask.

slide.description: A slide id, or a 1-based number.

tools.name: focus
tools.description: Zoom to an element or part right now and dim the rest, or clear focus. For choreography timed to speech, put [[focus ...]] cues in the narration instead.

target.description: element or element.part on the current slide; omit to clear.

region.description: [x, y, w, h] as fractions, to zoom somewhere that is not a named part. For images and diagrams these are fractions of the picture itself, the same space as callouts and inspect_image; otherwise of the element.

tools.name: say
tools.description: Speak and subtitle a line now, without adding it to the deck: 'One moment while I find photos of the mouth of the Nile.' Cues are allowed.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Answer the user in the chat box. For conversation and questions about what to do next; content belongs on slides.

tools.name: wait_for_user
tools.description: Wait for the user to do something: a chat message, a quiz answer, an 'ask about this' on part of a slide, or reaching the newest slide. Returns the events, or none after the timeout. Call it in a loop when you have nothing else to build.

tools.name: set_playback
tools.description: Work the controls the user has: play, pause or stop the performance, silence the voice, show or hide subtitles, and decide whether it runs on through the deck. After adding slides that answer a new question, play from the first of them through the last, so the user hears the answer and not the six slides they already sat through.

playback.description: play resumes or starts the slide on screen; stop silences everything until the user presses play.

from.description: A slide id: show it and perform from there.

through.description: A slide id: stop when its narration ends, instead of running on.

continuous.description: Move on by itself when a slide's narration ends.

muted.description: Silence the voice; slides and subtitles carry on.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: The user's settings: the voice, subtitles, pacing and the rest, with what each may be set to. Read before changing one, and to answer questions about how the app is set up.

tools.name: set_setting
tools.description: Change one of the user's settings, the same way the settings panel does. Only when they ask for it: these are the user's preferences, not yours, and the file they live in is theirs.

key.description: As get_settings lists it, e.g. narration.subtitles.

value.description: true, false, a number, or one of the values get_settings gives.

tools.name: describe_deck
tools.description: Look inside another saved presentation without opening it or disturbing the one on the stage: its slides, and the conversation that built it. For when the user refers to something you did in an earlier session.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: See the stage: a PNG of what the user sees, or of one slide. Use it to check a layout you are unsure of; it costs time, so not after every slide.

slide.description: A slide id; omit for the stage as it is now.

tools.name: inspect_image
tools.description: Look at an image with a labelled grid of fractions (0 to 1 across and down), so callout positions are measured, not guessed. Also returns its size, date, camera and location when known.

tools.name: scan_media
tools.description: List the images in a folder with their metadata (date taken, GPS, camera, size), for building galleries and timelines.
